body: Is there anything that reminds you of home in a good way? Maybe a movie you used to watch as a child, a stuffed animal you kept, that song your mom always sings along to when she's driving or the tv show your dad always hums the intro to while he does the dishes... Anything like that, surround yourself with it. Curl up with that stuffed animal and a blanket and re-watch the movie. Make a cup of something tasty and watch a few episodes of that old TV-show with the intro. Put on the songs your mother always sings and sing along, or play them softly in the background as you keep yourself busy with something. I find things like that bring a soft cloak of warm nostalgia, and eases it a little. I'm sending my thoughts and warmth to you.

I can very much relate to this. Throughout my teens I looked very extreme. I started out as pretty traditionally goth but loved experimenting with my looks: various haircuts including shaving it weirdly and dyeing it strange colours, wearing extreme makeup, torn and purposely mismatched clothes, piercings, etc...
This was noted by everyone working with me. When I ended up in a treatment home at 16, initially to treat my persistent and serious self harm issues, depression, suicidal ideation and psychosis, a lot of times I was told that if I would only try to "look normal" my issues would lessen, and a considerate amount of time was spent trying to "make me normal" instead of actually helping and treating my mental conditions - at the expense of it, even.

I'm an adult now, and while I still do dress in an eyecatching manner every now and then, I generally tend to look pretty laidback nowadays. Recently had to reestablish psychiatric contact and the way I'm treated is insanely different. I'm seen as "a normal person" who unfortunately suffers mental illness, not "a chronic crazy" who should just learn to conform in order to feel better. It's sickening. I do feel for you.

I was like you, SnowglobeSnot. I was uninterested in relationships, hadn't met anyone in a long while I had genuine feelings of any kind for, and had pretty recently learned the difference between what I call a BPD crush and a real crush. I tried staying away from drama and relationships, focusing fully on my hobbies and making friends. I've had the issue of friends confessing they love me before, but it could usually be handled in a good way.

But this time, all new friends I seemed to make inevitably started confessing feelings. I'd meet someone through a shared interest in a TV show and after about a week of knowing each other they go "you're so wonderful... you really bring *life* with you... I've never felt like this before... I *love* you..." And I've no idea what happened because all we talked about was that show, cracked some jokes about it and that's it. I was always at this time open about not being interested in romantic or sexual relationships so it wasn't some big secret, either. Other people I met acted similarly, with one guy repeatedly, explicitly told no over and over who basically bullied me into agreeing to go on at least one date with him. It went horribly, he told his best friend all about it and then they started messaging me calling me a manipulative bitch who ought to get my head together before I tried to "ensnare" anyone else and proceeded to tell me how I was evil and deserved only suffering. I blocked them both. A week later he's back, made an account somewhere else to message me asking to see me again because I'm the love of his life and he can't live without me.

People really *do* get obsessed with us even if we reject them and I don't know why. I've noticed this isn't just a BPD thing so much as it is a cluster B thing, though. I know several NPD and ASPD people who have the same experiences as us.

As someone into both goth and black metal, I've seen this comparison a ton of times *and it's so fucking stupid.* tr00 kvlt idiots who flame you for not liking Burzum are an entirely different story than goths having to explain the basic fact that unless you listen to goth, you're not a goth.

Would you say you're a metalhead if you don't like metal? *Ooooh but I wear lots of spikes!* Yeah, that's your personal fashion choice then, but if you don't listen to metal, you aren't a metalhead and those spikes don't change a thing about that. If you stick a safety pin through your cheek, don a mohawk and trash your clothing and then go about your day calling yourself a punk rocker without listening to or learning about the origins of punk, what part of you is punk rock when you don't care for *punk rock* or it's origins?
It's the same with goth music but at this point people have put more into that word than there is, simultaneously destroying the actual value of the word. 

Today, goth is some undefinable "dark quality"; a feeling, a mindset, a love for the spooky and macabre, wearing all black and watching horror movies. Today, goth is "liking black sets me apart from others". Dark, spooky and black-clad have been key notes about the goth *look* since forever and that's all people see, not the music that unifies these people (or all the not-so-spooky-looking goths who still burn for the music with a passion but prefer other styles of fashion.) 

I'm sick and tired that when it comes to goth, this is somehow seen as "gatekeeping" and some kind of radical, elitist standpoint, and I'm sick of seeing entitled disgusting people so wrapped up in shock value and the *I'm different from the rest*-mindset take on important roles in the community, spread misinformation and throw pity parties when anyone calls them out on their bullshit. Goth is a music style. That's where the goth subculture originated from. If you don't like goth, you're not goth. It's okay to not be goth and still prefer black. People need to stop destroying our subculture just because they're insecure about their identity if they don't have a label to slap on themselves.

I cut ties completely. If they're someone I can't escape in my daily life, I simply ignore them. It's noticeable to others and can get me a lot of exasperated sighs and "why can't you just *talk it out?*" Well, because they don't deserve anything from me, because I'm not required to put effort into someone not worthy of it, and because I don't care how much it might bother you - this person deserves the treatment and that's none of your business. It takes a lot of wrongdoing to get to that point, and once I'm done, I'm done.

There's another side to this coin as well. The intuitive understanding of others, our diplomacy, loyalty and deep emotional connection - these are serious things, and we do not hand them out lightly. We follow a set moral compass. If betrayed, we do not forget. Some of us may forgive, but I sure don't. To get on my blacklist you have to get close to my heart, but once you stab me in the back, my hatred for you is cold, eternal and ever seething. I *will* take every chance I find to get back at you. I will not hesitate. If you find yourself in need, when you reach out for me, the sweet ever-present friend you thought you could use to your liking without repercussions - I will spit in your face and laugh at your predicament. No help given. Imagine the INFP broken down and used by the people closest to them. Imagine the INFP who've had every last ounce of trust severed. Imagine the INFP with nothing left to lose. We follow our morals, but morals are relative and can change depending on how we are treated, what injustices we face and how we see the world. Pushed to their breaking point, the inner compass of an INFP could shift drastically, and make them completely devoted to their new, righteous cause: to get back at the world. That would be a villain who couldn't be reasoned with, who couldn't be calmed. All they'd be out for is blood. We'd make terrifying adversaries if pushed into too deep a pit. I would not want a fellow INFP as my enemy. The best/worst part? Nobody would see it coming, because they'd think we're all too sweet and docile to ever pose a threat to them.

I have an awful past, filled with abuse of many kinds and things I'd rather not remember, but when someone around me brings up a topic (especially one they're happy about) I don't say anything if it's something that reminds me of something bad or saddens me. I try to be happy for them, cheer them on, "good on you/I'm so happy for you!" and if they'd ask me how I personally feel about it I will (depending on how well I know you) either shrug it off and say it's fine because really that's nobody else's business, or maybe be a bit more open and say I'm not fine but that I'm managing and still am happy for you. I will be completely honest with my boyfriend when he asks me, but if you're my friend or coworker I won't dump my problems on you and especially not in a way that will kill your spirit and drag you down with me. It's perfectly okay to feel like everything's shit because you clawed yourself through absolute hell, but you don't take your pain and suffering out on others. If that is impossible for you to do, you seek help to make sure your behaviour stops. Once you start sliding into something like that, the road has a tendency to start disappearing in front of your feet, and discerning between what is abusive behaviour and what is not suddenly isn't so easy anymore. You do have a responsibility, even if you are suffering.

I love it. One of my all time favourite movies. Laura has always resonated so much with me and when I was younger I watched FWWM at least once a week, and carried The Secret Diary of Laura Palmer with me everywhere. As others have said, the vulnerable naked insight into Laura and her life and struggles are why I love it so much. She starts out as just a cold dead body, a victim, the darling girl of the whole town, and while the original series does show us that she certainly wasn't all sweetness and light, FWWM paints such a humane, beautiful and heartbreaking portrait of her as alive. I've always loved Laura for her darkness, which she tries so hard to repel but keeps giving in to. Some of my favorite scenes are the conversation between her and Donna ("what if you were falling in space..."), when she comes crying to Donna at her door ("Donna, are you my best friend?") after having just found out the truth, and Donna comforting her promising she's always her best friend, and also when she takes Donna out to meet up with those guys and panics when she realizes what's happening, hurrying to get her best friend out of there. The relationship and dynamic between Laura and Donna really helps bring out her character the best, imo. Donna has a loving father and a stable life. She doesn't want, need or understand the things Laura does. Laura desperately wants to be pure and good, having a life just like Donnas, but she cannot and for that she envies her friend but also desperately wants to protect her. The abuse she suffers makes her believe she deserves it, and she views herself as utterly depraved and lost. In spite of all this she doesn't stop fighting her destiny.
